deep.reconstruction:
This is folio 3v of the draft of Riemann's Göttingen Inaugural Dissertation (1851), 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse', §1. It matches the printed text almost word for word.

Context from the previous page. Let w = u + iv depend on z = x + iy, with dz = dx + i dy = ε e^{iφ}. Riemann decomposes the difference quotient:

dw/dz = ½(u_x + v_y) + ½ i(v_x − u_y) + ½[(u_x − v_y) + i(v_x + u_y)]·e^{−2iφ}.

In modern Wirtinger notation this is dw/dz = ∂w/∂z + (∂w/∂z̄)·(dz̄/dz), with dz̄/dz = e^{−2iφ}.

He then asserts (in the footnote *) that any w built from the elementary operations has dw/dz independent of dz. He says a strictly general proof is not needed, because the claim only motivates, and does not prove, what follows. The top of this page's footnote block finishes that sentence: '...werden kann, erfordert haben, und konnte hier ohne Nachtheil unterbleiben, da sie nur zur Motivirung, nicht zum Beweise des Folgenden dient.'

Main text (definition). This property is now taken as the definition. A 'Function einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse z' is any w that varies with z so that dw/dz is independent of dz. The justification of the definition is the investigation that follows, which develops the main common properties of such functions.

Implicit consequence (my addition, though it is immediate from the previous page): independence of φ means the coefficient of e^{−2iφ} vanishes. That is u_x = v_y and v_x = −u_y (the Cauchy–Riemann equations, ∂w/∂z̄ = 0). Then dw/dz = u_x + i v_x.

Footnote 1). Cauchy (session of the Paris Academy, 31 March of this year, i.e. 1851) understands a function w of z = x + yi as any quantity depending on z in a completely arbitrary way. Riemann grants that this is a legitimate choice in itself. He notes that it contradicts the concept previously attached to 'function of x+yi'. Once Cauchy later speaks of the derived function, i.e. the value of dw/dz at given z, the notion has no meaning. The reason is that dw/dz then takes different values according to the direction in which z changes, which is exactly the e^{−2iφ} term above.

There is no new computation on this page. It is definitional and polemical text.
errors: No mathematical errors. The asserted general claim, that every expression built from elementary operations is complex-differentiable, is left unproved. Riemann acknowledges this explicitly and uses it only as motivation. Strictly it also needs restrictions such as away from singularities and with a choice of branch.

results.what: Definition of a function of a complex variable as w(z) whose difference/differential quotient dw/dz is independent of the direction of dz (complex differentiability, equivalent to the Cauchy–Riemann equations).
results.modern_name: Holomorphic (complex-differentiable) function; Riemann's definition of analytic function via Cauchy–Riemann equations
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, Inaugural Dissertation 1851 (Cauchy–Riemann equations themselves go back to d'Alembert, Euler, Cauchy)

results.what: Critique of Cauchy's 31 March 1851 Comptes rendus usage of 'function of z' for arbitrary dependence: the derivative is then direction-dependent and meaningless.
results.modern_name: Distinction between general complex-valued functions and holomorphic functions (∂w/∂z̄ ≠ 0 gives direction-dependent derivative)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the draft of §1 of Riemann's published 1851 dissertation, including its well-known definition of complex functions and the footnote on Cauchy. Everything here is published and canonically attributed to him.

checkable.sympy: x,y,phi,eps=symbols('x y phi epsilon',real=True); u=Function('u')(x,y); v=Function('v')(x,y); dx=eps*cos(phi); dy=eps*sin(phi); lhs=(diff(u,x)*dx+diff(u,y)*dy+I*(diff(v,x)*dx+diff(v,y)*dy))/(dx+I*dy); rhs=Rational(1,2)*(diff(u,x)+diff(v,y))+Rational(1,2)*(diff(v,x)-diff(u,y))*I+Rational(1,2)*((diff(u,x)-diff(v,y))+(diff(v,x)+diff(u,y))*I)*exp(-2*I*phi); simplify(expand_complex(lhs-rhs))==0
checkable.asserts: Riemann's decomposition of the differential quotient (previous page) into a direction-independent part plus a part proportional to e^{-2iφ}.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y',real=True); w=expand((x+I*y)**3); u=re(w); v=im(w); [simplify(diff(u,x)-diff(v,y)), simplify(diff(v,x)+diff(u,y))]==[0,0]
checkable.asserts: A function built by elementary operations (z^3) satisfies the Cauchy–Riemann equations, so dw/dz is independent of the direction of dz.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y',real=True); u=x; v=-y; simplify(diff(v,x)+diff(u,y)+I*0), simplify(diff(u,x)-diff(v,y))
checkable.asserts: For w = conj(z) (an 'arbitrary' Cauchy-style dependence) u_x - v_y = 2 ≠ 0, so dw/dz depends on direction (equals e^{-2iφ}), illustrating the footnote's objection.

transcription_corrections: The footnote block's first three lines ('werden kann, erfordert haben, ... nicht zum Beweise des Folgenden dient.') are the continuation of footnote * from the previous page, not part of footnote 1). The transcription places them correctly but should mark them as such.
'ganz[?] d. h.' in the footnote: the word before 'd. h.' is uncertain in the image. It may be a struck or abbreviated word, possibly 'ganz' or 'gew.'. The sense is unaffected.
'Bewei-/se' is correctly read as 'Beweise'. 'Par. Ak.' = Pariser Akademie, and 'd. J.' = 'dieses Jahres' (1851).
